components.title: Guarded movement-failure task dispatch
components.summary: Routes the engine move-failure event to the current task only when one exists and is non-NIL; taskless tactical actors remain an explicit external-control state.

flows.title: Engine event to guarded task callback

steps.description: Decode the engine event, resolve the team unit and invoke UnitMoveFailed only for a known wrapper.
Ignore an already-stuck unit and retain the repeated-failure STOP, ROAM and reclaim-task branch.
Capture GetTask once and require a non-null, non-NIL task before dispatching the callback.
For an eligible task, compute a corrected radial escape position and issue a bounded move.

facts.statement: UnitMoveFailed captures the task once and calls OnUnitMoveFailed only when the pointer is non-null and the task type is non-NIL.
The ordinary task callback responds to movement failure with a corrected radial escape move under TRY_UNIT.
Tactical dispatch treats a null task as an actor with no Circuit scheduler handler and therefore already under external control.

For the documented taskless tactical state, the guarded branch removes the direct null-task dereference present in the earlier movement-failure callback path. This source inference does not establish native runtime acceptance.

open_questions: Will a genuine native run reproduce the taskless tactical movement-failure route without a crash?
Does the still-separate gateway OnUnitMoveFailed delta hook need production wiring for runtime observability?
